correctness.rationale: Every automorphism has matrix [[alpha,beta],[p^(b-a)c,delta]] with diagonal units. On G[p] the induced triangular map has columns (alpha_bar,c_bar) and (0,delta_bar). If alpha_bar !=1, delta_bar=1, the first fixed equation solves x and the remaining congruence has exactly p solutions iff E has valuation one; all such kernels lie on U_infty and count N1=p^(3a+b-3)(p−1)(p−2). If alpha_bar=1,delta_bar!=1 the second equation solves y, valuation-one condition for a>=2 (automatic a=1) counts N2; fixed socle slopes run uniformly over all t as c_bar varies, giving N2/p. If both diagonal residues 1, exact p-element kernel forces beta,c units and b-a=1; its p-element kernel is U_infty, counted N3=p^(4a-3)(p−1)^2. Disjoint cases give displayed formula. Independent full enumeration of automorphism matrices and all group fixed points for five small (p,a,b) cases reproduced each subgroup fiber including p=2 adjacent threshold. Nonenumerated p,a,b rely on valuation proof.
residual_risks: Counting proof assumes the known standard complete automorphism-matrix parametrization; the independent finite checks do not prove infinite formulas.

originality.rationale: Mozafar-Taeri classify which rank-two abelian p-group subgroups are Acentralizers but do not count the automorphisms over each line. Hayat et al count total theta(G,p), and a relevant prior published Resultary finding already proves the complete arbitrary-exponents theta(G,p) formula using these very same three residue cases. **Major overlap acknowledged:** the current result is not novel for the aggregate total or the case partition. Its distinct surviving content is the full ordered fiber distribution on all p+1 *individual* order-p subgroups, showing a distinguished long-factor line and uniform p finite lines, which aggregate counting does not state. This is a best-of-knowledge narrow but real refinement.

value.rationale: Fixed-subgroup fibers refine the natural Acentralizer existence problem, distinguish the characteristic socle line from other order-p subgroups, and quantify the exact p=2 exceptional restriction. Unlike only counting fixed-point totals, they answer which particular subgroup is fixed by how many automorphisms; the complete family is a useful group-action invariant, despite using the prior theta proof case split.
residual_risks: No distribution over larger subgroups or higher-rank groups follows.

final_claim: For all primes p and exponents 1<=a<b in G=C_{p^a}⊕C_{p^b}, every finite-slope order-p socle subgroup U_t has m_G(U_t)=p^b(p−2) if a=1, or p^(3a+b−4)(p−1)(p−2) if a>=2; long-factor line U_infty has m_G(U_infty)=p^(3a+b−3)(p−1)(p−2)+1_{b=a+1}p^(4a−3)(p−1)^2. For p=2 only long line may occur, precisely for adjacent exponents.
limitations: Only order-p fixed subgroups, 1<=a<b and arbitrary prime p.
Novelty is in the distribution among individual socle lines, not the earlier exact total theta(A,p) formula.
